title: ATP Finals 2026: Draw, format and schedule as Carlos Alcaraz sets Alexander Zverev in his sights
content:
At this year’s ATP Finals in Turin, Italy, a new world No. 1 is trying to fend off a resurgent generational talent — and the defending champion is nowhere to be found.

Alexander Zverev goes into the season-ending event for the best eight singles players and doubles pairs of the year on top of the singles rankings, after winning two Grand Slam titles in 2026. Snapping at his heels is Carlos Alcaraz, who returned from a right wrist injury at the U.S. Open and has won two tournaments in a row going into Turin.

Missing is home hero Jannik Sinner, the biggest star in Italy and the two-time defending champion. A right knee injury has kept Sinner off the court since his Wimbledon title this summer, and it’s his absence, alongside that of Alcaraz, in which Zverev has seized the top ranking.

Joining Sinner and Alcaraz are four debutants, in the shape of Italy’s Flavio Cobolli, France’s Arthur Fils, Frances Tiafoe of the U.S. and Spain’s Rafael Jódar, who is the first man to reach the event in the same year that he made his ATP Tour debut.

Ben Shelton of the U.S. and Russia’s Daniil Medvedev complete the field.

Here’s everything you need to know about the tournament, with the schedule and results to be updated as it gets underway from Nov. 15.

The eight players who qualified were split into four pots for the draw. Pot 1 is No. 1 and No. 2, Pot 2 is No. 3 and No. 4, and so on.

These seedings follow the players’ rankings in the ATP Race to Turin, a table that counts only ranking points earned in 2026.

Each player then plays three round-robin matches. The top two players from each group contest the semifinals, with the winners meeting in the final.

🇩🇪 Alexander Zverev (1)

🇺🇸 Ben Shelton (3)

🇫🇷 Arthur Fils (6)

🇪🇸 Rafael Jódar (8)

🇪🇸 Carlos Alcaraz (2)

🇷🇺 Daniil Medvedev (4)

🇮🇹 Flavio Cobolli (5)

🇺🇸 Frances Tiafoe (7)

🇫🇮 Harri Heliövaara and 🇬🇧 Henry Patten (1)

🇸🇻 Marcelo Arévalo and 🇭🇷 Mate Pavić (4)

🇫🇷 Theo Arribage and 🇫🇷 Albano Olivetti (6)

🇧🇷 Orlando Luz and 🇧🇷 Rafael Matos (8)

🇺🇸 Christian Harrison and 🇬🇧 Neal Skupski (2)

🇪🇸 Marcel Granollers and 🇦🇷 Horacio Zeballos (3)

🇮🇹 Simone Bolelli and 🇮🇹 Andrea Vavassori (5)

🇩🇪 Kevin Krawietz and 🇩🇪 Tim Puetz (7)

The tournament starts Nov. 15. There are six days of round-robin competition, with two singles matches and two doubles matches per day. The singles matches are played second and fourth, starting at 8 a.m. ET and not before 2:30 p.m. ET. The doubles matches start at 5:30 a.m. ET and 12 p.m. ET.

On Nov. 21, it is semifinal day, with the first singles match starting half-an-hour later than the round robin and the second again not before 2:30 p.m. On Nov. 22, the singles championship match will start at 12 p.m.

There is global coverage on the ATP’s streaming service, Tennis TV, as well as Tennis Channel in the U.S. and Sky Sports in the U.K.

Harri Heliovaara / Henry Patten (1) vs. Orlando Luz / Rafael Matos (8)

Alexander Zverev (1) vs. Rafael Jódar (8)

Marcelo Arévalo / Mate Pavić (4) vs. Theo Arribage / Albano Olivetti (6)

Ben Shelton (3) vs. Arthur Fils (6)

Marcel Granollers / Horacio Zeballos (3) vs. Simone Bolelli / Andrea Vavassori (5)

Carlos Alcaraz (2) vs. Frances Tiafoe (7)

Christian Harrison / Neal Skupski (2) vs. Kevin Krawietz / Tim Puetz (7)

Daniil Medvedev (4) vs. Flavio Cobolli (5)

Sinner won the singles title at the 2025 ATP Finals, also held in Turin. He defeated Alcaraz 7-6(4), 7-5 in the final, winning all five of his matches at the event. The title earned Sinner just over $5 million.

In the doubles, Henry Patten of Great Britain and Harri Heliövaara of Finland defeated Joe Salisbury and Neal Skupski, both from the U.K, 7-5, 6-3. They split just under $863,000.

This year’s prize pool is $15.75 million. It is allocated per match win and structured so the champions in singles and doubles take home the biggest prize if they go through the event undefeated with five wins (three round-robin wins, a semifinal win, and then victory in the final). An undefeated singles champion will win $5.17 million.

Last year’s prize pool was $15.5 million.

The winner of the singles final will receive just over $2.4 million, while the winner of each semifinal will receive just over $1.2 million; the prize for a round-robin match win is $405,000 and each singles player receives $338000 just for appearing at the event, provided that they play all three of their round-robin matches.

The winning doubles pair will receive $959,300 if they go undefeated.

Round-robin wins carry 200 points, a semifinal win carries 400 points and a final win carries 500 points. An undefeated champion (three round-robin wins, a semifinal win and a final win) will earn 1,500 points.
